basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 22-23.' and it opens 'VERS. 22, 23.-- Et fuerunt filii Lothan Bosri, et Emman, et soror Lothan Tamna. Haec est'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 22, 23.-- Et fuerunt filii Lothan Bosri, et Emman, et soror Lothan Tamna. Haec est autem | Tamna, de qua supra dictum est: et Tamna concubina erat Eliphaz, filii primogeniti Esau, et ex ipsa natus est Amalech. Idcirco autem Corraeorum recordatus est, quia primogenitus filiorum Esau ex filiabus eorum acceperat concubinam. Quod autem dicitur: Theman, et Cenef, et Amalech, et reliqua, sciamus postea regionibus Idumaeorum ex his vocabula imposita.
